entities.name: Anthropic
entities.does: The Claude models

entities.name: ATLAS
entities.does: General-purpose proton collisions — Higgs properties and searches for new particles
notable: Co-discovered the Higgs boson in 2012
Has published thousands of measurements and searches since
Being rebuilt now for the High-Luminosity LHC

entities.name: Blue Origin
entities.does: New Shepard suborbital flights and New Glenn
notable: New Shepard has flown crew on suborbital hops since 2021
New Glenn reached orbit on its first flight, January 2025
Building the Blue Moon lunar lander for NASA's Artemis programme

entities.name: Euclid
entities.does: Surveying a third of the sky to map how dark energy stretched the universe
notable: First survey images, November 2023
First bulk data release, 2025 — the survey is meant to run six years

entities.name: Hubble
entities.does: Optical and ultraviolet astronomy — still the sharpest UV eye we have
notable: The Deep Field (1995): point at nothing, find thousands of galaxies
Pinned down the expansion rate, and started the tension over its value
Still working after 35 years and five servicing missions

entities.name: ISS
entities.does: Continuously crewed laboratory — microgravity science and the testbed for everything that follows
notable: Continuously crewed since November 2000
AMS-02 has been mounted outside since 2011
The testbed for every commercial crew and station programme that follows

entities.name: JWST
entities.does: Infrared astronomy — the earliest galaxies
notable: First images released July 2022
Galaxies seen further back than any telescope had reached
CO2 detected in an exoplanet atmosphere (WASP-39b), a first
The TRAPPIST-1 rocky planets, checked for air

entities.name: OpenAI
entities.does: GPT models
notable: GPT-3 (2020) then ChatGPT (2022), which moved the field into public view
The API most consumer AI products are built on

entities.name: Rubin Observatory
entities.does: Will image the whole southern sky every few nights for ten years
notable: First-look images released June 2025
Will repeat the whole southern sky every few nights for ten years
Expected to multiply the number of known solar system objects

entities.name: SpaceX
entities.does: Falcon 9 and Starship launch vehicles
notable: Falcon 9: first orbital-class booster landing in 2015, now routine and reflown
Dragon: first commercial crew flight, Demo-2, in 2020
Starship: full flight tests since 2023, booster caught by the tower in 2024
Starlink: by far the largest satellite constellation ever operated
Launched Europa Clipper for NASA in October 2024

entities.name: ActInSpace
entities.status: every two years — 2026 finals in Bordeaux
entities.does: A 24-hour contest to turn a real space patent into a business idea

entities.name: AI Security Institute
entities.does: State-run evaluations of frontier models for dangerous capabilities

entities.name: AI2
entities.does: Fully open models — weights

entities.name: ALICE
entities.does: Heavy-ion collisions — the quark-gluon plasma that filled the early universe

entities.name: ALPHA
entities.does: Trapped antihydrogen — whether antimatter obeys the same spectroscopy and gravity as matter

entities.name: AMS-02
entities.does: Cosmic ray composition from space — searching for antimatter and dark matter signatures

entities.name: Arc Institute
entities.org: non-profit, with Stanford, UCSF and Berkeley
entities.does: Where AI and biology meet as one lab: genome language models built next to the wet benches that test them.
notable: Its Evo models read and write DNA across all domains of life
Used a genome language model to design working bacteriophages
Funds scientists for years at a time, not grant cycles

entities.name: Astroscale
entities.does: Rendezvous with and removal of dead satellites and debris — the orbital cleanup business
notable: ELSA-d demonstrated magnetic capture of a client satellite in 2021
ADRAS-J flew right up to a discarded Japanese rocket stage in 2024 and photographed it
Working toward actually removing debris, not just approaching it

entities.name: Belle II
entities.does: Electron-positron collisions at the Upsilon(4S) — B meson decays and flavour anomalies

entities.name: BioNTech
entities.does: Founded to make cancer immunotherapy, became famous for a vaccine, and has gone back to cancer.
notable: Co-developed the first authorised mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, with Pfizer
Founders Uğur Şahin and Özlem Türeci started it for cancer, not viruses
Oncology pipeline now includes bispecific antibodies

entities.name: Broad Institute
entities.full_name: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
entities.does: Genomics at industrial scale, and the lab behind base editing and prime editing.
notable: Base and prime editing now in more than 25 clinical trials
gnomAD has contributed to over 13 million genetic diagnoses
Has sequenced nearly 900,000 whole human genomes

entities.name: Caltech SURF
entities.status: annual — proposals due in the winter
entities.does: A summer of research at Caltech or JPL, written up and defended like a real project — students propose the work themselves.
notable: Running since 1979
Students write their own proposal with a mentor
JPL projects are part of the same programme

entities.name: CERN Summer Student
entities.status: annual — applications close in the winter
entities.does: Eight to thirteen weeks on a real project at CERN, with a lecture series alongside it. Paid: a net allowance of 94 CHF per day, health insurance, and travel costs in some cases.
notable: For bachelor's and master's students with at least six semesters done
Physics, engineering, computer science and maths
One of the few places an undergraduate works inside a running experiment

entities.name: CMS
entities.does: General-purpose proton collisions — the independent cross-check on ATLAS

entities.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
entities.does: A compact tokamak made possible by high-temperature superconducting magnets — the magnets are the whole bet.
notable: SPARC is designed to be the first commercially relevant machine to produce net fusion energy
ARC, the power plant meant to follow it, is already sited
The largest private fusion company by funding

entities.name: Copernicus Masters
entities.does: Prizes

entities.name: CRISPR Therapeutics
entities.does: Makes the first approved CRISPR medicine: patients' own stem cells, edited and returned.
notable: Casgevy, developed with Vertex, is approved for sickle cell disease and beta thalassaemia
Co-founded by Emmanuelle Charpentier
The first time gene editing became a prescription

entities.name: DESY Summer Students
entities.does: Seven and a half weeks inside a major accelerator laboratory, on photon science, accelerators, particle or astroparticle physics.
notable: 2026 edition ran 21 July to 10 September
Free hostel accommodation plus a daily stipend, travel partly reimbursed
Open to undergraduates in physics and related fields

entities.name: EleutherAI
entities.does: Grassroots open-source research collective; released open models when almost nobody else did

entities.name: ESA Business Incubation
entities.does: Funding

entities.name: ESA Young Graduate Trainee
entities.does: About 100 one-year paid traineeships a year for people finishing a master's degree

entities.name: Europa Clipper
entities.does: Will fly close passes over Europa to test whether its subsurface ocean could be habitable
notable: Launched October 2024 on a Falcon Heavy
Mars gravity assist, March 2025
Will make dozens of close passes rather than orbit Europa — radiation would kill it

entities.name: Exotrail
entities.does: Electric thrusters and an orbital transfer vehicle — the tow truck that moves satellites
notable: spacevan, an orbital transfer vehicle, has flown
ExoMG Hall thrusters fly on other operators' smallsats
Sells the manoeuvre, not the hardware — mobility as a service

entities.name: FASER
entities.does: Very forward particles — collider neutrinos and long-lived light particles

entities.name: Fervo Energy
entities.does: Geothermal power anywhere hot rock is deep enough, using the horizontal drilling and fibre sensing the oil industry perfected.
notable: Signed a 396 MW power purchase agreement with Google, September 2026
Building Cape Station in Utah
Staffed deliberately with oil and gas engineers

entities.name: Firefly Aerospace
entities.does: Alpha launch vehicle and the Blue Ghost lunar lander
notable: Blue Ghost Mission 1 landed upright on Mare Crisium in March 2025
Alpha is its small launch vehicle
One of the few commercial landers to reach the Moon intact

entities.name: Google DeepMind
entities.does: Gemini
notable: AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in 2016
AlphaFold predicted protein structures at scale; its authors shared a Nobel in 2024
Gemini is the production model line

entities.name: Google Summer of Code
entities.does: Twelve weeks contributing to an open-source project with a mentor from that project, stipend included. Several scientific-software organisations take part each year.
notable: Over 21,000 contributors since 2005, across 1,000+ organisations
Astropy, the HEP software projects and similar groups participate regularly
Contact the organisation before the proposal window — that is what decides selection

entities.name: Helion
entities.does: Pulsed magneto-inertial fusion that aims to turn the plasma's energy straight into electricity, skipping the steam turbine.
notable: Polaris: the first privately built machine to show measurable deuterium-tritium fusion
Raised $465 million in June 2026 at a $15.5 billion valuation
Building Orion, which it calls the first fusion power plant

entities.name: Hugging Face
entities.does: The public hub where models and datasets are shared — the field's distribution layer

entities.name: IAI Space
entities.does: Observation and communications satellites
notable: Ofek reconnaissance satellites, launched on Israel's own Shavit rocket
The Amos communications satellite series
Built the Beresheet lander with SpaceIL
One of about eleven organisations worldwide with end-to-end space capability

entities.name: IceCube
entities.does: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos
notable: Found the first high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, 2013
Traced one 2017 event back to a flaring blazar
Mapped neutrino emission from the plane of our own galaxy, 2023

entities.name: ICEYE
entities.does: Small radar satellites that image through cloud and darkness
notable: Put the first smallsat synthetic-aperture radar in orbit
Its flood maps are used by insurers and disaster response
Radar sees through cloud and at night, which optical imaging cannot

entities.name: ICTP Trieste
entities.full_name: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics
entities.does: Schools, workshops and a diploma year in theoretical physics, aimed particularly at scientists from countries without that training at home.
notable: Founded by Abdus Salam to keep physics from concentrating in rich countries
Most schools cover travel and accommodation for accepted participants
Work here fed into neutrino oscillation theory and climate modelling

entities.name: ImageSat International
entities.does: High-resolution observation satellites and the analysis layer on top of them
notable: Operates the EROS high-resolution observation satellites
GEOIMPACT layers AI analysis over the imagery
Sells sovereign capability, not only pictures

entities.name: Intuitive Machines
entities.does: Nova-C lunar landers flown under NASA's commercial lunar payload programme
notable: IM-1 Odysseus, February 2024 — the first US soft landing since Apollo, though it tipped over
IM-2 Athena followed in March 2025
Flies under NASA's commercial lunar payload programme

entities.name: Isomorphic Labs
entities.org: Alphabet, spun out of Google DeepMind
entities.does: AlphaFold's successors, pointed at drug design instead of structure prediction.
notable: Led by Demis Hassabis, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel for AlphaFold
Co-developed AlphaFold 3 with Google DeepMind
Drug-discovery partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies

entities.name: JUICE
entities.does: Will study Ganymede
notable: Launched April 2023
First ever Moon-then-Earth double gravity assist, August 2024
Venus flyby 2025; Jupiter arrival planned 2031

entities.name: KATRIN
entities.does: The neutrino mass directly

entities.name: LHCb
entities.does: Beauty and charm quark decays — matter/antimatter asymmetry and flavour anomalies

entities.name: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA
entities.does: Spacetime ripples from merging black holes and neutron stars
notable: GW150914 (2015): the first direct detection, two black holes merging
GW170817 (2017): a neutron star merger seen in gravitational waves and in light
The O4 observing run has pushed the catalogue past 200 candidate events

entities.name: LZ
entities.does: Direct dark matter detection — XENONnT's main competitor and cross-check

entities.name: Meta FAIR
entities.does: Open-weight Llama models and a large share of the field's published research

entities.name: Mila
entities.does: One of the largest academic deep learning groups

entities.name: Mistral AI
entities.does: Europe's frontier lab

entities.name: Moderna
entities.does: Medicines written as mRNA: instructions the body's own cells follow to make the protein that does the work.
notable: COVID-19 vaccine, 2020
Its mRNA flu vaccine was approved by the FDA in August 2026
Personalised cancer vaccines built from each patient's tumour are in late-stage trials

entities.name: NA62
entities.does: The ultra-rare kaon decay K+ to pi+ nu nubar — one of the sharpest tests of the Standard Model

entities.name: NASA Space Apps Challenge
entities.does: A weekend hackathon on real agency data; local events run in Israel and across Europe

entities.name: NIF
entities.does: 192 laser beams crush a fuel capsule until it fuses — the only laboratory on Earth to have reached ignition.
notable: December 2022: more fusion energy out than laser energy in, a first anywhere
2.05 MJ of laser light produced 3.1 MJ of fusion yield
Ignition has since been repeated at higher gain

entities.name: Oxford PV
entities.org: private, spun out of Oxford University
entities.does: Perovskite layered on silicon — two cells in one, each catching the part of sunlight the other wastes.
notable: Built on Henry Snaith's perovskite research
Among the first to put perovskite-silicon tandems into commercial modules
Tandems are how solar gets past the single-junction efficiency limit

entities.name: Parker Solar Probe
entities.does: Flying through the Sun's corona to find out what heats it and accelerates the solar wind
notable: First spacecraft to fly through the Sun's corona, 2021
Closest approach December 2024, about 6.1 million km from the surface
Fastest object ever built by humans

entities.name: Perseverance
entities.does: Roving an ancient river delta and caching samples for a future return mission
notable: Carried Ingenuity, which flew 72 times before its rotor was damaged in 2024
Sample tubes cached at Three Forks, waiting for a return mission
Found organic molecules in Jezero's delta rocks

entities.name: Pierre Auger Observatory
entities.does: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays — where the most energetic particles in nature come from

entities.name: Planet Labs
entities.does: Images the entire landmass of Earth daily with a fleet of small optical satellites
notable: The Dove flock images Earth's entire landmass daily
SkySat adds high-resolution tasking on top of that baseline
Archive now spans more than a decade of daily coverage

entities.name: Ramon Foundation
entities.does: Israel's space education pipeline — school programmes

entities.name: Ramon.Space
entities.does: Radiation-tolerant computers for spacecraft — supercomputing that survives orbit
notable: Radiation-tolerant processors that keep working through orbital radiation
Aimed at moving real computation off the ground and into the spacecraft
Opened US engineering operations near Denver

entities.name: Rocket Lab
entities.does: Electron small launcher
notable: Electron reached orbit in 2018 and is the busiest small launcher
Launched CAPSTONE to lunar orbit for NASA in 2022
Recovers boosters from the sea to study reuse
Neutron, a larger reusable vehicle, is in development

entities.name: SolarEdge
entities.does: The electronics between a solar panel and the grid — optimisers and inverters that get more out of every roof.
notable: Installed in more than 140 countries
Leads in rooftop solar capacity
Moved into home storage and grid services

entities.name: StemRad
entities.does: The AstroRad vest
notable: AstroRad flew on Artemis I around the Moon, on the MARE experiment
Also tested aboard the ISS
Shields bone marrow selectively rather than the whole body

entities.name: StoreDot
entities.does: Silicon-anode batteries built to charge an electric car in minutes rather than hours.
notable: Extreme-fast-charging cells at 300 Wh/kg
Partnerships with Mercedes, Volvo and Polestar
Backed by bp and TDK

entities.name: T2K
entities.does: Neutrino oscillation and hints of CP violation in the lepton sector

entities.name: TerraPower
entities.does: Natrium, a sodium-cooled fission reactor with molten-salt storage bolted on — so the plant can surge when the grid needs it.
notable: First plant under construction in Wyoming
345 MWe, with over five hours of molten-salt energy storage
Also developing medical isotopes for cancer treatment

entities.name: Voyager 1 and 2
entities.does: The only working instruments humanity has outside the Sun's bubble
notable: Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space in 2012, Voyager 2 in 2018
Engineers recovered Voyager 1 from a failed memory chip in 2024, from 24 billion km away
Instruments are being switched off one by one to stretch the power budget

entities.name: Weizmann Institute
entities.does: One of the world's leading basic-science institutes, strong in immunology, cancer and the gut microbiome.
notable: Its ILLUMINE team won up to £20m in Cancer Grand Challenges, 2025
Pioneering work linking gut microbes to immunity
Research here led to several of Israel's best-known drugs

entities.name: Wendelstein 7-X
entities.org: Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics
entities.does: The largest stellarator ever built — a twisted magnetic bottle designed to hold plasma continuously rather than in pulses.
notable: First plasma in December 2015; 50 superconducting coils, none of them a simple shape
Built to sustain discharges up to 30 minutes
Reaches confinement comparable to tokamaks without their pulsed limit

entities.name: XENONnT
entities.does: Direct dark matter detection — a WIMP recoiling off a liquid xenon nucleus

entities.name: XRISM
entities.does: High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy — the motion of hot gas around black holes and clusters
notable: Resolve spectrometer reads gas motion around black holes to a few km/s
First science results released 2024

canon.title: Achievement of Target Gain Larger than Unity in an Inertial Fusion Experiment
canon.why: 2.05 MJ of laser light in, 3.1 MJ of fusion out. Seventy years of trying, finally over the line.

canon.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
canon.why: A fifty-year-old problem, largely solved. The structures are free for every known protein.

canon.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
canon.why: GPT-3. The paper where scaling alone started producing abilities nobody trained for.

canon.title: Attention Is All You Need
canon.why: The transformer. Every large language model in use today is a descendant of this one paper.

canon.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger
canon.why: Spacetime itself was measured ringing, a century after Einstein said it would.

canon.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
canon.why: Skip connections made very deep networks trainable. Almost everything since is built on them.

canon.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
canon.why: Two networks trained against each other — the idea that made generated images convincing.

canon.title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson
canon.why: The last missing piece of the Standard Model, found 48 years after it was predicted.

canon.title: A Programmable Dual-RNA–Guided DNA Endonuclease in Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
canon.who: Jinek, Chylinski, Fonfara, Hauer, Doudna and Charpentier
canon.why: CRISPR-Cas9 turned from a bacterial immune system into a tool for editing any genome.

canon.title: Suppression of RNA Recognition by Toll-like Receptors
canon.why: The modified-nucleoside trick that stops the body attacking mRNA. Ignored for years, then it made the COVID vaccines work.

canon.title: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe
canon.why: The expansion is speeding up, and nobody knows why. Dark energy is the name for not knowing.

canon.title: Evidence for Oscillation of Atmospheric Neutrinos
canon.why: Neutrinos change type as they travel, which means they have mass — the Standard Model said they did not.

canon.title: LixCoO2: A new cathode material for batteries of high energy density
canon.why: The cathode inside the lithium-ion battery in your phone. A Nobel, 39 years later.

canon.title: The hippocampus as a spatial map
canon.why: The discovery of place cells — the brain's internal map. Nobel Prize 2014.

canon.title: Self-Consistent Equations Including Exchange and Correlation Effects
canon.why: The practical form of density functional theory — how most of computational chemistry works today.

canon.title: A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s
canon.why: They thought it was pigeon droppings in the antenna. It was the afterglow of the Big Bang.

canon.title: Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex
canon.why: How the visual cortex builds edges and shapes out of spots of light — and an inspiration for convolutional networks.

canon.title: Detailed Balance Limit of Efficiency of p-n Junction Solar Cells
canon.why: Why a single solar cell tops out near a third of the sunlight it catches — and why tandems exist.

canon.title: Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay
canon.why: Nature tells left from right. Physicists had assumed for decades that it could not.

canon.title: Synthesis of the Elements in Stars
canon.why: How every element heavier than helium got made. The paper that ties nuclear physics to the sky.

canon.title: Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor
canon.why: How hot, how dense and for how long — the bar every fusion machine is still measured against.

canon.title: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid
canon.why: One page, and the double helix. Built on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data, which she was not told they had.

canon.title: A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve
canon.why: The equations for how a neuron fires. Still the basis of every realistic neuron model.

canon.title: Über den Nachweis und das Verhalten der bei der Bestrahlung des Urans mittels Neutronen entstehenden Erdalkalimetalle
canon.why: The chemistry showing uranium had split into barium. They could not explain it, and published anyway.

canon.title: Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction
canon.why: The explanation Hahn could not give, worked out over a winter walk. Meitner was left off the Nobel.

canon.title: The Nature of the Chemical Bond
canon.why: Quantum mechanics turned into the chemist's everyday picture of bonds and hybrid orbitals.

canon.title: A relation between distance and radial velocity among extra-galactic nebulae
canon.why: Two and a half pages showing the universe is expanding. Cosmology starts here.

watch.name: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
watch.why: Nine lectures building a working GPT from nothing, in code, with every line explained.

watch.name: Neural networks
watch.why: The visual explanation of what a network is actually doing. Start here if the maths looks opaque.

watch.name: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
watch.why: Top-down: you train a working model in lesson one and learn why it worked afterwards.

watch.name: Short courses (agents, RAG, evaluation)
watch.why: Short, current, built with the labs themselves — though the catalogue has moved to a membership.

watch.name: Paper walkthroughs
watch.why: Reads the week's papers out loud and argues with them, which is how you learn to read them yourself.

watch.name: PBS Space Time
watch.why: The rare channel that keeps the real equations in and still stays followable.

watch.name: Dr. Becky
watch.why: A working astrophysicist walking through the month's results, including the ones that did not hold up.

watch.name: Fermilab
watch.why: Particle physics explained by the lab that does it, without the press-release gloss.

watch.name: Cool Worlds
watch.why: A working exoplanet astronomer thinking out loud about habitability and how we would ever know.

watch.name: Anton Petrov
watch.why: A short, careful video on almost every new astronomy result, usually within days of the paper.

watch.name: Kurzgesagt
watch.why: The most beautiful science animation being made, and the sources are published alongside each video.

watch.name: Deep Sky Videos
watch.why: Real astronomers talking through objects one at a time, telescope time included.

watch.name: Event Horizon
watch.why: Long interviews with the researchers themselves — where cosmology arguments actually get made.

watch.name: Scott Manley
watch.why: Orbital mechanics and launch failures explained by someone who reads the telemetry.

watch.name: Astrum
watch.why: Built from real probe imagery — what the spacecraft actually sent back, not an artist's impression.

books.title: Bayesian Data Analysis
books.who: Gelman, Carlin, Stern, Dunson, Vehtari and Rubin
books.why: How to reason about uncertainty when you have a model and not much data. Free PDF from the authors.

books.title: Numerical Recipes
books.why: The algorithms behind the library functions you call, explained well enough to know when they will fail you.

books.title: Statistical Data Analysis
books.why: The standard reference for how physicists actually handle errors, fits and limits. Short, and nothing wasted.

books.title: Data Reduction and Error Analysis for the Physical Sciences
books.why: The first statistics book most physics students meet, and the one they keep going back to.

books.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
books.why: If you are going to publish plots, read this before you publish more of them.

books.title: An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics
books.why: The standard undergraduate course in one very heavy volume — stars, galaxies, cosmology, all of it.

books.title: Introduction to Cosmology
books.why: The clearest first cosmology book there is. You can read it end to end without getting stuck.

books.title: Black Holes and Time Warps
books.why: Written before LIGO detected anything, by the person who argued it would. Worth reading for that alone.

books.title: The First Three Minutes
books.why: A Nobel laureate walking through the early universe minute by minute, without hiding the physics.

books.title: Liftoff
books.why: How SpaceX nearly died before Falcon 1 reached orbit. Reported, not mythologised.

books.title: Reentry
books.why: The sequel: Falcon 9, reuse, and the decisions that turned a survivor into the whole market.

books.title: Space Mission Analysis and Design
books.why: The engineering reference the industry actually sizes missions with. Known simply as SMAD.

books.title: The Right Stuff
books.why: Why anyone climbs onto a rocket at all. Still the best writing about test pilots and nerve.

books.title: Modern Particle Physics
books.why: The current standard course. Works the calculations through instead of quoting results.

books.title: Introduction to Elementary Particles
books.why: Griffiths explains things the way a good supervisor would. Start here before Thomson.

books.title: Review of Particle Physics
books.why: Every measured property of every known particle, updated yearly and free. The field's single most-used document.

books.title: Lost in Math
books.why: An argument that beauty has been a bad guide in theoretical physics. Contested, and worth arguing with.

books.title: Plasma Physics and Fusion Energy
books.why: What it would actually take to build a fusion reactor, with the engineering constraints left in.

books.title: The Making of the Atomic Bomb
books.why: A Pulitzer for a book that is also a genuine history of 20th-century nuclear physics. Read it for Meitner and Bohr.

books.title: Midnight in Chernobyl
books.why: Reactor physics as it behaves when institutions fail. The clearest account of what actually happened.

books.title: Deep Learning
books.why: The foundations, from linear algebra up. Free online, and still the reference for why things work.

books.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
books.why: Bridges classical statistics and deep learning in one framework. Draft PDF free, code in Python and JAX.

books.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
books.why: By the people who built the field. Free PDF, and still the clearest treatment of the basics.

books.title: The Alignment Problem
books.why: The honest version of why making these systems do what we meant is hard, told through the research.

books.title: Sustainable Energy — Without the Hot Air
books.why: Every energy argument turned into kilowatt-hours per person per day. Free online, and it settles a lot of arguments.

books.title: Molecular Biology of the Cell
books.why: The textbook of cell biology. If you come from physics, this is where the vocabulary comes from.

books.title: The Gene
books.why: From Mendel to gene editing, written by an oncologist with a family history that makes it personal.

books.title: The Code Breaker
books.why: Jennifer Doudna and the race to CRISPR, with the rivalries left in.

items.abstract: We report the first measurement of the semileptonic decay D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 μ + ν μ and an improved measurement of the decay D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 e + ν e using a sample of 7.33 fb − 1 of e + e − annihilation data collected at center-of-mass energies between 4.128 and 4.226 GeV with the BESIII detector at the Beijing Electron Positron Collider (BEPCII). We measure the branching fractions to be B ( D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 μ + ν μ ) = ( 2.07 ± 0.2 2 stat ± 0.1 0 syst ) × 10 − 3 and B ( D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 e + ν e ) = ( 2.14 ± 0.1 8 stat ± 0.1 0 syst ) × 10 − 3 . Based on a simultaneous study of the dynamics in two semileptonic decays, the hadronic form factor parameters in the D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 transition are determined to be r V = V ( 0 ) / A 1 ( 0 ) = 1.63 ± 0.1 4 stat ± 0.0 8 syst , r 2 = A 2 ( 0 ) / A 1 ( 0 ) = 0.60 ± 0.1 3 stat ± 0.0 6 syst , and A 1 ( 0 ) = 0.56 ± 0.0 2 stat ± 0.0 1 syst , where V ( 0 ) is the vector form factor and A 1 , 2 ( 0 ) are the axial-vector form factors evaluated at q 2 = 0 . The precision of r V and r 2 is improved by twofold and A 1 ( 0 ) is measured for the first time. We also report the first model-independent measurements of the differential decay rates and the lepton forward-backward asymmetries for D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 ℓ + ν ℓ decays. Based on these measurements, we perform a test of lepton flavor universality in full and separate q 2 intervals with D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 ℓ + ν ℓ decays. No violation is found within uncertainties. Our results present for the first time a complete study of the dynamics in the D s + → K * ( 892 ) 0 transition, and provide stringent tests of various nonperturbative theoretical calculations.

items.title: NASA's Pandora SmallSat Mission: Gaussian Processes for Simulated Stellar Heterogeneity Corrections under Imperfect Stellar Models
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Stellar contamination is the primary bottleneck limiting robust atmospheric characterization of exoplanets orbiting active K- and M-dwarfs with James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) transmission spectroscopy. Launched in January 2026, NASA's Pandora SmallSat mission addresses this challenge through long-term, simultaneous visible photometry and near-infrared spectroscopy of planet-hosting stars, providing the data to disentangle planetary and stellar signals. However, conventional stellar-contamination corrections rely on stellar atmosphere models, making them vulnerable to model inaccuracies that can impede accurate inferences. Here, we investigate how Pandora data can be used to mitigate stellar contamination without an accurate host star model. We present a Gaussian-process-aided stellar retrieval framework that learns wavelength-dependent deviations from current stellar model grids. We propagate stellar contamination factors directly from the stellar retrieval into the planetary atmospheric retrievals, allowing the atmospheric inference to marginalize over stellar-contamination uncertainty without relying on a biased stellar model. Tests using simulated Pandora observations with realistic stellar model mismatch show that this framework consistently improves the recovery of disk-integrated stellar spectra. For a WASP-69 b-like system, this approach can reduce model-driven biases in inferred atmospheric properties, though degeneracies among stellar and atmospheric parameters can leave residual biases. This flexible, data-driven framework is a promising approach toward accurate stellar-contamination corrections and more robust atmospheric inference even when host-star model grids are inaccurate.

items.title: Black hole accretion flows as dark matter bolometers
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Astrophysical systems provide powerful probes of dark matter interactions, complementing direct-detection searches. We propose using accretion flows of the supermassive black hole as a bolometer for light DM. The kinetic energy of sub-MeV dark matter in the black hole gravitational potential can remain below the thermal energy of the plasma electrons. The colder dark matter population can therefore absorb energy through elastic scattering, cooling the electrons and modifying their emission spectrum. We integrate dark matter cooling into the advection-dominated accretion flow around M87$^{*}$ and solve the full set of thermodynamic equations to obtain the resulting temperature profile and radio-to-millimeter emission. By comparing the predicted spectrum with observations accompanying the Event Horizon Telescope campaign, we use, for the first time, the thermal energy balance of the hot accretion flow to constrain DM-electron scattering, obtaining stringent limits on keV-to-MeV DM for both heavy and light mediators.

items.title: An oxygen-rich supernova remnant in NGC 253 with narrow [N II] emission lines
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Context. Supernova remnants (SNRs) are the final evolutionary stage of supernovae. In rare cases, the remnant persists as an optically luminous remnant decades after the explosion. We report the discovery of an unusual oxygen-rich (O-rich) SNR that was serendipitously discovered in the MUSE mosaic of the nearby (D $\sim$ 3.5 Mpc) galaxy NGC 253 released by arXiv:2506.14921. Aims. We search for SNRs in MUSE integral field spectroscopy data of NGC 253. Methods. We search for unresolved point sources with broad and strong [O III]$λ$$λ$4959,5007, [O I]$λ$$λ$6300,6364 or [O II]$λ$$λ$7320,7331 emission lines. We also search for possible counterparts at other wavelengths in archival data. Results. We find a single O-rich SNR in NGC 253 with [O III]$λ$$λ$4959,5007. For this object, we report a coincident X-ray source detected by Chandra and a non-detection at mid-infrared wavelengths by JWST. Additionally, we identify [N II]$λ$$λ$6548,6583 emission lines and no detectable hydrogen or [SII]$λ$$λ$6716,6731 emission. The [N II] emission lines are broader (230 km/s) than the surrounding interstellar medium lines but still narrow in comparison to the [O III] emission (>1500 km/s) from the SNR. No detections of [O I]$λ$$λ$6300,6364 and [O II]$λ$$λ$7320,7331 were made. Conclusions. The discovery of a single O-rich SNR after a systematic search of NGC 253 highlights their scarcity in nearby galaxies. The structure of [O III] emission indicates complex structure in the O-rich ejecta. The relative narrowness of [N II] emission lines compared to the [O III] lines and the non-detection of hydrogen show that the remnant is surrounded by an N-rich circumstellar medium. The ejecta is currently interacting with this material of the preceding supernova explosion.

items.title: A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients from extragalactic sources. Their frequency and polarization properties are affected by plasma and magnetic fields along the line of sight to Earth. We report radio observations of FRB 20240304B and near-infrared follow-up to identify its host galaxy. The host is a low-mass, clumpy, star-forming galaxy at redshift 2.148 ± 0.0013, corresponding to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. This FRB occurred during the peak of cosmic star formation and probes ionized gas over ~80% of cosmic history. The highly scattered burst emission implies that there is a population of FRBs that are undetected by current surveys.

items.title: MINDS: The mid-infrared spectrum of the disk, jets, and winds of DG Tau
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: DG Tau is one of the best-studied young stellar objects in transition from a Class I protostar to a T Tauri star. It is no longer embedded in a dense molecular cloud, but still reveals features that are commonly seen in protostars at earlier evolutionary stages. DG Tau hosts a protoplanetary disk and two energetic jets that can be studied down to the immediate environment of the star and disk at optical, infrared, and X-ray wavelengths. We use the Medium Resolution Spectrometer of MIRI on the James Webb Space Telescope. DG Tau's mid-infrared spectrum consists of a very bright continuum with various silicate features, and lines of CO, H$_2$O, OH, H I, H$_2$, Ne$^{+}$, Ne$^{2+}$, Ar$^{+}$, Fe$^{+}$, and Ni$^{+}$. We find substantial grain growth to at least 2 $μ$m at an early evolutionary stage. Lines of H$_2$O and CO are formed at extremely high temperatures (600-2000 K). The ratio of warm to hot water is the lowest among previous observations of disks with JWST. This and a very strong continuum point toward the relevance of the strong accretion of DG Tau and consequently strong stellar UV irradiation. The pair of jets reveals a rich spectrum of emission lines from ions, in particular producing forbidden lines of [Ne II], [Ne III], [Ar II], [Fe II], and [Ni II]. The forward jet shows a collimated structure as found previously, while the hitherto poorly described, receding jet is more widely dispersed on scales of several arcsec, showing a layered structure with the fastest components being the most collimated. The ionization of the jet gas cannot be reconciled with high-energy radiation from the star itself. Instead, we propose a unified nonequilibrium ionization shock model in which the previously studied X-ray jet plasma continuously cools, recombining ions until, at temperatures around $10^4$ K and below, metals at low ionization stages emit the observed ion lines.

items.title: Discovering Warped Extra Dimensions at Next Generation Dark Matter Detectors
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The coming years will see what could be the final push in the search for WIMP dark matter (DM), with direct detection reaching into the neutrino fog and indirect detection reaching TeV-scale thermal relics. We study a class of models that these experiments could discover: DM emerging from a warped extra dimension. In the IR, these scenarios appear generically as a $Z'$-type portal. We show that DM with electroweak couplings and TeV scale masses remains viable and discoverable within such a bottom-up context. However, the models require a 20\% tuning between the DM and $Z'$ masses, a tuning that is relaxed if the DM and $Z'$ are strongly coupled and heavier ($\sim$$10$ TeV). In fact, it is the strongly-coupled $Z'$-type portal which is UV-completed by the framework of a warped extra-dimensional Grand Unified Theory (GUT), where DM stability is a spin-off of suppressing proton decay, resulting in a $\sim$$10$ TeV Kaluza-Klein (KK) scale. We identify a variant of this framework where all gauge fields except a baryon-number gauge boson have suppressed couplings to the DM; this model significantly suppresses the direct detection rate, but it remains discoverable through indirect detection. Further, to address the little hierarchy problem associated with $\sim$$10$ TeV KK scale, inspired by the Super-Composite Higgs, we augment our extra-dimensional GUT setup with supersymmetry. We show that this model also possesses a DM candidate, now with a weakly-coupled and $\sim$${\rm TeV}$ mass $Z'$ mediator. In all cases, a near-term discovery remains possible, for instance with the now online Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO), suggesting that our first hint of extra dimensions could emerge from the high-energy sky.

items.title: Stereodivergent telomerization of linear functionalized dienes with amines
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Despite the importance of divergent synthesis to obtain different isomers for medicinal and material chemistry, divergent stereocontrol over four distinct selectivity factors remains a fundamental challenge. The telomerization reaction is limited to the transformation of simple unfunctionalized 1,3-dienes to circumvent intractable stereoisomeric mixtures. Here, we report an orthogonal telomerization platform using linear functionalized 1,3-dienes as the substrates, which simultaneously dictates geometric, regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivities. We prepared diverse types of γ-amino esters from identical, readily available unsaturated esters and amines via synergistic palladium and acid catalysis, with each precisely obtained out of hundreds of potential telomers. We developed several chiral phosphoramidite ligands to promote the transformation. This study showcases the potential of multidimensional stereomanipulation for the industrially valuable telomerization reaction.

items.title: Integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance for high-resolution tracking of measles virus evolution and transmission
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Measles outbreaks have surged globally, challenging surveillance and control efforts. In South Africa, the 2024−2025 measles outbreak led to nearly 4,000 reported cases, triggering a nationwide vaccination campaign. However, tracking measles virus (MeV; species Morbillivirus hominis ) transmission and evolution remains difficult at scale, particularly in settings with limited access to care, diagnostic testing and sequencing capacity. Wastewater can enable population-scale virus surveillance, but low MeV concentrations limit detection sensitivity and sequencing quality. Here we show that overcoming these technical challenges enables integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance that expands the coverage and resolution of MeV monitoring. We developed a virus concentration and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) workflow and applied it to 4,502 wastewater samples collected across all nine provinces of South Africa during the 2024−2025 outbreak. Wastewater MeV genotype prevalence tracked clinical estimates, and phylogenetic analyses combining wastewater and clinical sequences revealed geographically structured transmission and previously undetected inter-provincial spread. WGS recovered transmission links not captured by the field standard approach, which targets a 450-nucleotide region of the nucleoprotein gene (N450), highlighting the importance of WGS to accurately characterize transmission dynamics. Our study provides a cost-effective and scalable genomic surveillance approach to support measles control and elimination.

items.title: Certification of quantum correlations at arbitrary distances through routed Bell tests
items.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated on each paper page)
items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2288 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-11-27-2288 Transmission loss represents a major obstacle to the device-independent certification of quantum correlations over long distances, limiting applications such as device-independent quantum key distribution (DIQKD). In this work, we investigate the recently proposed concept of routed Bell experiments, in which a particle sent to one side can be measured either near or far from the source. We prove that routed Bell tests involving only entangled qubits can certify quantum correlations even in the presence of arbitrary loss on the channel to the distant device. This is achieved by adapting concepts from self-testing and quantum steering to the routed Bell test framework. Finally, as a natural extension of our approach, we outline a DIQKD protocol that, in principle, is secure over arbitrary distances. Talk at QCrypt2025 based on this manuscript.

items.title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Heterochromatin typically represses genes 1,2 , yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation 3–7 . How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent 8 . In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly 8 . By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

items.title: Differential active adhesion and a capillary instability drive global eversion and dissemination of bacterial colonies
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Attractive forces between cells can determine the shape and sorting behaviour of bacterial colonies. During colony development, chemical gradients form within the colony, but it is unclear how they affect cohesion. Here we discover that such gradients trigger global eversion of proliferating colonies formed by the human pathogen Neisseria gonorrhoeae . Like a jet, the inner core flows towards the periphery where it is partially dispersed and partially spreads around the core of the colony. Living dispersed cells reform colonies, leading to rapid dissemination. The eversion depends on local oxygen depletion, which reduces the activity of the molecular motors that govern self-attraction: before the eversion, the colony consists of a weakly cohesive spherical core surrounded by a strongly cohesive shell. An idealized computational model reveals that, in this configuration, an instability analogous to a capillary instability emerges when the thickness of the strongly interacting shell falls below a critical value. We show that the probability for eversion strongly depends on the motor-generated attractive force between bacteria. Overall, our results indicate that chemical gradients induce spontaneous symmetry breaking in a mechanically active colony, thereby triggering a nonlinear shape instability. This instability generates large-scale cellular fluxes that redistribute bacteria towards environments more favourable for their growth.

items.title: Precision Positronium Spectroscopy as a Test of the Helium Ionization Energy Anomaly
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Precise measurements of the metastable helium ( 1 s ) ( 2 s ) S 3 1 ionization energy have revealed a 9 σ discrepancy with QED theory that persists in isotopic measurements, suggesting a leptophilic bosonic interaction as a possible explanation. A subsequent investigation has suggested that only a scalar boson interaction would be consistent with the He observations. In addition to electron-electron interactions this kind of mediator can also be expected to give rise to electron-positron interactions, and may therefore also affect positronium (Ps) atoms. To quantify this we derive the response of Ps energy levels to the corresponding finite-range Yukawa potential, using exact hydrogenic matrix elements and a numerical helium calculation. Across the viable mediator-mass range of 0–800 eV, the He anomaly interpreted in this way implies a positronium 1 S 1 3 → 2 S 1 3 shift ranging from 0.250–0.850 MHz, and a 2 S 1 3 ionization shift of 0.140–0.210 MHz. We discuss the feasibility of observing these shifts experimentally.

items.title: AI-based digital pathology defines spatial border ecosystems in triple-negative breast cancer
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The invasive tumor border in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is currently poorly understood. We integrated digital pathology and spatial multi-omics to define border ecosystems in TNBC. AI-based digital pathology identified five border ecosystems, three associated with prognosis. Spatial multi-omics analyses further resolved the spatial niche, molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance of these ecosystems. Immune-infiltrated borders contain a triadic immune niche associated with favorable prognosis and immunotherapy sensitivity. Tumor–stroma borders harbor a MIF + fibroblast exclusion niche that blocks immune infiltration and suppresses T cells function, predicting poor prognosis. Tumor–adipose borders, featured an FLT1 + endothelial niche, promote hypoxia, vascular leakage, and tumor dissemination. Targeting this niche inhibits tumor progression. Collectively, these findings establish a spatial resource that might enable border-directed therapeutic strategies in TNBC.

items.title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

items.title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. We describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which uses free-atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges, from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active-site architecture that incorporates a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases, we obtained active catalysts in zero-shot 96 construct design campaigns.

items.title: Rebuilding science’s social contract with the public
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Much has been written about how the social contract between science and society in the United States is in crisis. According to its terms, research will yield broad economic, health, and security benefits to the very public that funds it. But this relationship depends on public trust in science, its systems, and the scientists themselves, and therein lies the problem. Beyond making discoveries and publishing results, scientists shape their own culture, and that is where some changes may be the key to rebuilding public trust.

items.title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multiomics, including metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides, across 1543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multiomic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas–informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune-repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

items.title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

items.abstract:
We report a background characterization for the search for two-neutrino double-beta ($2
u2β$) decay of $^{160}$Gd using Ce:Gd$_3$Al$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$ scintillators in the PIKACHU experiment Phase 1 at the Kamioka underground laboratory. The experimental backgrounds were investigated through delayed-coincidence analysis and spectral fitting based on GEANT4 simulations. No significant excess attributable to $^{160}$Gd $2
u2β$ decay was observed, yielding a lower limit of $T^{2ν}_{1/2} \geq 2.32 	imes 10^{19}$ yr at 90\% C.L. The established background model and analysis framework provide a foundation for future PIKACHU phases aiming to discover $^{160}$Gd $2
u2β$ decay.

items.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($δ$) is 0 or $π$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $ν_μ$ and $ν_τ$, but not the $ν_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sinδ$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. The confusion arises from an improper T test that subtracts a probability from itself: a mathematical identity, not a physics result. In this paper, we clarify the distinctions between a proper and an improper T test as well as the proper and improper CP and CPT tests, for a general, arbitrary matter profile. For a toy model consisting of two different layers of constant density, we find that the maximum T-violation is obtained when one layer is close to the solar resonance, and the other is close to the atmospheric resonance. We address whether the matter asymmetry for DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments is sufficiently large to allow the $\sinδ$ dependence to be probed in $ν_μ$ survival probability. We also discuss future experimental scenarios that could probe T/CP-violation in $ν_μ$ survival probability.

items.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated on each paper page)
items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2287 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-11-27-2287 We present ffsim, an open-source software library for fast simulation of fermionic quantum circuits. ffsim exploits conservation of particle number and the z component of spin, symmetries present in a wide range of fermionic systems, to dramatically reduce memory usage and simulation time compared to general-purpose quantum circuit simulators. Compared to $\textsf{FQE}$, a library with similar functionality, $\textsf{ffsim}$ differs in software design and is faster on a representative set of simulation benchmarks. Beyond state vector evolution by basic fermionic gates, $\textsf{ffsim}$ offers a number of additional features including variational ansatzes, Hamiltonian time evolution via Trotter-Suzuki product formulas, efficient sampling of Slater determinants, seamless integration with $\textsf{Qiskit}$ and $\textsf{PySCF}$, and comprehensive documentation. We demonstrate ffsim's capabilities on scientific applications, including a 64-qubit Hubbard model with 8 electrons. $\textsf{ffsim}$'s source code and documentation are available via GITHUB .

items.title: Decoding Multimode Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Codes with Noisy Auxiliary States
items.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated on each paper page)
items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2286 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-11-27-2286 In order to achieve fault-tolerant quantum computing, we make use of quantum error correction schemes designed to protect the logical information of the system from decoherence. A promising way to preserve such information is to use the multimode Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) encoding, which encodes logical qubits into several harmonic oscillators. In this work, we focus on decoding the measurements obtained from Steane-type quantum error correction protocols for multimode GKP codes. We propose a decoder that considers the noise present on the auxiliary states, more specifically by tracking the correlations between errors on different modes spreading throughout the error-correction circuit. We show that leveraging the correlations between measurement results and the actual error affecting the multimode GKP state can decrease the logical error probability by at least an order of magnitude, yielding more robust quantum computation.

items.title: Letter of Intent: AN Underground Belayed In-Shaft (ANUBIS) detector
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Long-lived particles (LLPs) arise naturally in many extensions of the Standard Model, notably in models with dark matter candidates or motivated by baryogenesis. LLPs produced at or above the electroweak scale with decay lengths of tens of metres escape the general-purpose LHC detectors and cannot be produced at sufficient rates in forward and beam-dump experiments. This Letter of Intent proposes the ANUBIS detector, which would instrument the ceiling of the ATLAS cavern and the bottom of its access shafts with about 1600~m$^2$ of resistive plate chambers in two tracking layers about 1~m apart, using the air-filled volume above the ATLAS detector as decay volume. The ANUBIS detector exploits the full ATLAS event information to suppress backgrounds, and exchanges triggers with the ATLAS experiment. With 3~ab$^{-1}$ at the High-Luminosity LHC, it would improve the sensitivity to exotic Higgs-boson decays into long-lived scalars by two to three orders of magnitude, probe heavy neutral leptons of all three flavours down to mixings of about $2\times10^{-8}$, and extend the reach for axion-like particles. The \textsl{pro}ANUBIS demonstrator, operated in the ATLAS cavern in 2024 and 2025, has validated the detector technology. The detector design, trigger concept, integration with the ATLAS experiment and a timeline towards installation in LHC Long Shutdown 4 are presented.

items.title: Neural-Network Approximators for Low-Thrust Multi-Asteroid Rendezvous Optimization
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Designing low-thrust multi-asteroid rendezvous missions requires the coupled selection of asteroid sequences, encounter epochs, and low-thrust trajectories. Lambert transfers support rapid beam search but do not directly describe thrust-limited transfer capacity or propellant consumption. This paper develops two complementary low-thrust neural approximators. The first directly predicts the continuous maximum admissible initial mass from numerically optimized low-thrust transfers, providing a transfer-capacity estimate for comparison with the current spacecraft mass. The second predicts mass-dependent propellant consumption and propagates spacecraft mass to subsequent legs. With the carefully-designed input features and network structure, the approximators reduce mean absolute errors by 72.2% and 75.5%, respectively, relative to conventional deep neural network baselines. These predictions are incorporated into a Lambert-ranked beam search through resource filtering and recursive mass propagation before final beam selection. The method is evaluated on fixed-visit, maximum-visit, and deployment-collection missions. Across the tested cases, the proposed resource filtering increases the fraction of candidate sequences that yield accepted low-thrust solutions, raises the maximum validated asteroid-visit count by up to 15.4%, and improves the best mission objective by up to 17.8%. These results demonstrate that continuous transfer-capacity and propellant predictions can improve finite-width sequence search.

items.title: The nature of the Norma arm as a bar-driven star-forming shock front
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The Milky Way is commonly depicted as having four main spiral arms, including the Norma–outer arm, and a central stellar bar whose properties remain debated. Masers associated with young high-mass stars have been used to trace a segment of the ‘Norma arm’ extending from one end of the Galaxy’s central stellar bar. Recent work suggests that these masers may reside along a spiral arm or occupy the dominant x 1 stellar orbits that give the bar its shape. Here we use a new generation of N -body, hydrodynamic simulations to argue that these million-year-old masers instead trace the Galactic bar’s quadrant I shock front or, equivalently, its dust lane. This implies that the bar dust lane is star-forming, shedding new light on our understanding of star formation processes in the Milky Way. By associating the masers with the simulated shock front, we determine the parameters of the bar to be: a ≈ 4.3 ± 0.2 kpc, b ≈ 2.3 ± 0.2 kpc, ϕ = $${{20}_{-2}^{+5}}^{\circ }$$ 20 - 2 + 5 ∘ and Ω p ≲ 40 km s −1 kpc −1 , representing the semimajor and semiminor half-lengths of the bar, the inclination angle and the pattern speed, respectively. This raises questions about the Milky Way’s spiral structure and suggests that the Galactic bar is long, slow and star-forming.

items.title: Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Interfacial void formation during discharge limits the practical performance of lithium metal solid-state batteries. Here we show that introducing an egg-box topography at the Li/Li 6 PS 5 Cl interface increases the discharge current at which voiding commences tenfold, from 0.2 to 2 mA cm −2 at 2 MPa and 30 °C. The contoured interface also sustains pulsed currents up to 3 mA cm −2 at 30 °C and 8 mA cm −2 at 60 °C without cell failure. Under these conditions, it does not completely eliminate void formation but suppresses void growth and associated voltage polarization. Consequently, it sustains discharge profiles derived from the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure, representing realistic electric vehicle driving demands, whereas non-contoured interfaces fail rapidly. A full cell with a thin contoured solid electrolyte retains this advantage over its non-contoured counterpart. Contouring the Li/solid electrolyte interface is therefore an effective strategy for enabling practically relevant discharge rates in solid-state batteries.

items.title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Voice agents in shared spaces must satisfy interdependent multi-user requests while upholding per-user authority, privacy, and task constraints. Existing evaluations offer limited coverage when participants react throughout a session. We introduce $μ$-Bench, a benchmark for joint task completion in closed-loop, full-duplex multi-user voice interaction. Simulated participants act from isolated profiles of goals, knowledge, and permissions, adapting to the agent's speech and tool outcomes. Across 20 domains, 100 scenarios vary group size, acoustics, and follow-up demands to form 800 cases (408 tool-augmented, 392 tool-free). Joint Task Success (JTS) requires all user goals, privacy boundaries, and terminal states to hold jointly, while Pure JTS further disallows unauthorized tool calls; Attribution, Threading, and Coordination (ATC) diagnostics localize failures. Across 13 voice agents, proprietary systems peak at 62.24\% tool-free and 65.44\% tool-augmented success, while open-weight models remain below 20\%. ATC diagnostics show that open-weight models lag primarily in multi-turn attribution and threading, and controlled contrasts reveal that larger groups consistently degrade joint task success across capable systems. By coupling reactive multi-user simulation with verifiable session-level outcomes, $μ$-Bench provides a rigorous testbed for shared voice agents.

items.title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one. A well-established framework, rooted in the work of Davies and operationalised for particle physics by Gross and Vitells, provides this correction for scans over continuous parameters. Some aspects, however, remain unsettled. The definition of "elsewhere" is ambiguous and ranges from a single distribution to an entire experimental programme. Moreover, the analytical shortcuts of the classical framework do not carry over to searches based on machine learning (ML), which are affected by an implicit post-selection bias that depends on the model's resolution and expressiveness. This review covers the LEE in searches for new physics at colliders, from its statistical foundations to these modern challenges. We discuss the corrections for continuous scans and for multiple discrete tests, illustrated with simple numerical examples, and the interaction between ML and the LEE, which we connect to the broader literature on selective inference. We highlight open problems, including the computational cost of empirical calibration for complex models and the development of analytical shortcuts for ML test statistics, and offer recommendations for reporting discovery significance in both classical and ML-based searches in particle physics.

items.title: Stranger Things: When Objects Appear Without Their Typical Neighbors
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Visual context is a powerful cue for object recognition: scenes inform what, where, and at what scale objects are likely to appear. Yet over-reliance on context becomes a failure mode when models predict objects based on their typical neighbors rather than the objects' own visual features, which we call typicality bias. While extensively studied in the pre-Transformer era, it has often been assumed that architectural and scale improvements would naturally solve it, and a systematic diagnostic across the modern vision stack remains absent. We provide such a diagnostic framework. We measure typicality bias via normalized pointwise mutual information (NPMI) over object pairs, and introduce STRANGE-Bench (Synthetic Typicality-RANked Grounded Evaluation Benchmark): a photorealistic, layout-controlled benchmark spanning 17 sub-tiers from typical to never-co-occurring object pairs. Across five model families (specialist detectors, open-vocabulary detectors, self-supervised, vision-language, and multimodal large language models) and three recognition tasks (supervised detection, open-vocabulary detection, and classification), the bias is prevalent: gaps of 5-11 p.p. persist when objects appear outside their typical company, and do not consistently shrink with scale. To mitigate it, we turn to data augmentation: existing augmentations are designed for visual diversity, not for breaking co-occurrence shortcuts, and sample from the very distribution that produces typicality bias. We propose Anchor-Atypicality Sampling (AAS), a simple sampling rule for paste-based augmentations that uses the NPMI signal to tilt the training-time co-occurrence distribution toward atypical partners. AAS reduces the typicality gap by up to 1.6 p.p. on natural-image COCO splits and 23.0 p.p. on synthetic STRANGE-Bench across three model families, without sacrificing overall performance.

items.title: A 2D fluid model in BOUT++/Hermes-3 for simulating detached divertor plasmas in tokamaks
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Detached divertor operation is essential for controlling target heat fluxes in future high-power tokamaks. We present a two-dimensional fluid model implemented in BOUT++/Hermes-3 for simulating detached divertor plasmas with plasma-neutral interactions and fixed-fraction impurity radiation. We report improvements to the PETSc SNES-based steady-state solver used for two-dimensional axisymmetric transport simulations with fluid neutrals and assess the performance of several sparse-solver preconditioning strategies. For the cases considered here, STRUMPACK used as an ILU preconditioner with low-rank compression provides the most favorable performance, reducing the linear-to-nonlinear iteration ratio and achieving approximately a fivefold speedup relative to \HYPRE{}-based configurations. The optimized solver is then applied to DIII-D shot $\#174287$ at 4000~ms to characterize detached divertor conditions. Cross-field transport coefficients are adjusted to reproduce upstream experimental profiles, and detachment is modeled using nitrogen fixed-fraction radiation. Steady-state particle and energy balances are evaluated by decomposing the density and pressure equations into their transport and source terms. In the outer divertor, electron energy losses are dominated by ionization and impurity radiation, while ion energy losses occur mainly through collisional transfer to electrons. An upstream separatrix density scan shows decreasing target electron temperature and a rollover of the integrated target ion saturation current at higher $n_{e,\mathrm{sep}}$ consistent with expected detachment trends. These developments establish a foundation for future multispecies simulations. Hermes-3 is publicly available on GitHub under the GPL-3 open-source license.

items.title: Applying functional MRI analysis techniques to whole-brain calcium-imaging data to investigate structural and functional relationships in Drosophila melanogaster
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Clarifying the relationship between structure and function is important for understanding the brain. In Drosophila melanogaster , FlyEM and FlyWire electron microscopy-based connectome data, and whole-brain calcium-imaging data are available. We applied pre-processing methods from functional magnetic resonance imaging to whole-brain calcium-imaging data and comprehensively investigated the optimal parameters. Then, we found that the FC–SC (functional and structural connectivity) correlation decreased linearly with region of interest count, and this trend was the same in flies and humans. We also developed a new, more robust method to quantify the degree of pre- and post-synaptic segregation, and investigated this in the fly whole-brain. This revealed that many neurons have unsegregated synapses. We extracted highly unsegregated synapses and compared them with random-extracted null SC matrices. Their FC–SC correlation was significantly higher, indicating that these synapses contribute to FC well. Conversely, highly segregated synapses showed significantly lower FC–SC correlation and contribute less to FC. Neurons with unsegregated synapses, like non-spiking neurons, are spread throughout the whole-brain, and they are thought to have a significant influence on FC.

items.title: Direct lineage conversion of postnatal mouse cortical astrocytes to oligodendrocyte lineage cells
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Oligodendrocyte lineage cells (OLCs) are lost in many central nervous system (CNS) diseases. Here, we investigate the generation of new OLCs via ectopic expression of Sox10 , Olig2, or Nkx6.2 in mouse postnatal astrocytes. Using stringent analyses, including Aldh1l1-astrocyte fate mapping and live-cell imaging, we confirm that Sox10 and Olig2 , but not Nkx6.2 , convert Aldh1l1 pos astrocytes to induced OLCs (iOLCs). With single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), we uncover the molecular signatures of iOLCs. Finally, perturbation models CellOracle and Fatecode support the idea that Sox10 drives cells toward a terminal iOLC fate. Altogether, this multidimensional analysis shows bona fide conversion of astrocytes to iOLCs using Sox10 or Olig2 and provides a foundation for astrocyte direct lineage reprogramming (DLR) strategies to promote OLC repair.

items.title: Butterfly Effect in Kinetic Plasma Turbulence
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The butterfly effect is a fundamental process in chaotic systems, but it has not previously been characterized in detail for a collisionless turbulent plasma. In this work, we apply particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of driven turbulence to study the emergence of the butterfly effect from a small initial perturbation to the simulated particles. In particular, we compare pairs of (baseline and perturbed) simulations that differ only by a localized initial perturbation (down to the single-particle level). We find that the effect of the localized perturbation spreads radially throughout the PIC simulation, causing a difference between each simulation pair that is exponentially amplified over time within the affected region. The fields, including the electric current density, eventually become statistically decorrelated. We construct an analytical model combining spatial expansion with exponential amplification to approximate the early-time evolution. Varying the initial perturbation primarily affects the early-time evolution, while having little effect on the final, decorrelated state. We describe parameter scans with varying plasma beta and temperature (covering sub-relativistic and ultra-relativistic regimes). Our results show that remarkably small perturbations will grow to decorrelate each pair of simulations within a few dynamical times; the imposed perturbation can no longer be resolved once it falls below the numerical precision floor set by the machine precision. These results confirm that the butterfly effect is very strong and robust in a collisionless plasma, with implications for the predictability of turbulent plasma systems.
